I farm only 6 mu, so I will keep the plan steady and labor-efficient. I have 28 years in the field, a six-person household, and well irrigation, so I do not need to gamble on a complicated change this year. I will keep cabbage and chili as my main line because that fits my usual cabbage-chili system and matches what I know how to manage well. I will still keep some eggplant and kidney bean, but on smaller area, so I can spread labor, cash flow, and risk. For seed, I will use hybrid seed for cabbage, chili, and eggplant because on a small farm I care more about stable stand, uniformity, and marketable yield than saving seed. For kidney bean, I will use improved seed rather than pushing fertilizer too hard, because bean does not need as much nitrogen and I mainly want a reliable crop with lower input. I will use rotary tillage on all plots because it is practical for my scale and lets me prepare land quickly at the start of the season. With well water, I will irrigate on time instead of waiting for rain, especially for cabbage and the fruiting vegetables. I will keep fertilizer moderate to strong on cabbage, chili, and eggplant, lighter on kidney bean, and I will spray pesticides based on pressure but keep cabbage and chili tighter because they are more exposed to insect and disease losses here. This is the kind of plan I would actually follow myself: not too risky, not too light, and aimed at stable output from all 6 mu.
